commitResults.messageBody: Install the project-specific HTML diff workflow and its bundled generator so future code increments can be reviewed in a self-contained split view.

commitResults.messageTitle: mark as done without the classes

commitResults.messageBody:
Task descriptions and completion states are managed separately in Dog,
which makes the data easy to desynchronize and leaves task behavior in the
command loop.

Introduce Task to own its description and completion state. Move both Java
classes into the dog package and update the run instructions to match. This
keeps each task's data and behavior together while satisfying the project
coding standard.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add SE-EDU Java coding standard skill
commitResults.messageBody:
Java changes need a consistent project-wide convention, but the rules are
not available to the agent between tasks.

Add a project-specific skill summarizing the authoritative SE-EDU rules and
mandate its use in AGENTS.md. This keeps future Java work consistent while
linking back to the maintained source.

Commit messages and branch names need consistent conventions across future
work.

Add a project-specific skill summarizing the SE-EDU Git rules and mandate its
use in AGENTS.md. This makes focused, reviewable history the default for
future repository changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Completed lvl 4 without inheritance for now
Add fail-fast console UI testing workflow
commitResults.messageBody:
Chatbot changes need repeatable checks with visible input and output.
Ad hoc runs do not reliably expose regressions between increments.

Add a test-ui skill, an executable test plan, and a command-by-command
runner that stops at the first mismatch. Require agents to review the
plan and run the skill after code changes so failures remain visible.

The command loop mixes task operations with detailed output formatting.
This makes the workflow harder to scan and nests the nonempty list path.

Extract named display methods and guard the empty-list case early.
Follow the course guidance on logical structure and a single level of
abstraction without changing the console output or adding new classes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Separate command routing from task operations
commitResults.messageBody:
The main loop still combines input, dispatch, index validation and task
mutation. Readers must hold all these details in mind at once.

Extract focused routing and status-update methods, and report command
errors at the loop boundary. Keep task state local and return its count
explicitly, following the course guidance on short methods and scope.

Deadline and event parsing repeat split, trim and validation logic.
The generic parts names and long creation method hide field meanings.

Extract task-specific creation methods and share required-field checks.
Name the parsed fields and centralize usage messages, following the
course guidance on duplication and names that explain their purpose.
Expand UI coverage for malformed and free-form date fields.

The inheritance increment referenced Todo, Deadline, and Event without
tracking their source files, so a clean checkout could not compile.

Add the missing subclasses and document the task hierarchy so later
increments build from a complete, standards-compliant baseline.

Malformed commands previously produced inconsistent guidance without the
chatbot's normal visual framing. Unknown commands also lacked the Level 5
error style.

Display all validation failures consistently, provide command-specific
messages, and extend the UI plan with unknown-command coverage.

The task hierarchy shared the application package, which mixed the
program entry point with domain classes as the codebase grew.

Move Task and its subclasses into dog.task while keeping Dog in the
top-level dog package. This preserves the existing entry point and keeps
the source-root layout compatible with project tools.

Users need to remove obsolete tasks while retaining continuous list
numbering. Invalid delete requests must also preserve the task list.

Validate the requested task number, shift later array entries forward,
clear the unused slot, and report the removed task and updated count.
Extend UI coverage for successful and invalid deletions.

The fixed-size array required manual task counts, capacity checks, and
element shifting during deletion. Those details obscure the task-list
operations and impose an unnecessary size limit.

Use ArrayList<Task> so additions, removals, indexing, and size tracking
are handled by the Java Collections API while preserving UI behavior.

Task data was lost whenever the chatbot exited, preventing users from
continuing their list in a later session.

Store tasks under the relative, cross-platform data/dog.txt path and
reload them at startup. Preserve task types, details, and completion
status, create missing directories, and skip corrupt records safely.
Extend the UI plan with deterministic preload and corruption coverage.

# Conflicts:
#	src/main/java/dog/Dog.java

Dog mixes command execution with task construction and input validation.
This makes parsing rules harder to locate and change independently.

Move task-field parsing, related errors, and task-number conversion into
a stateless Parser class. Keep execution and persistence in Dog for this
first incremental extraction, preserving all existing console behavior.

Validate with the test-ui skill: all five cases pass on Java 25,
including malformed fields, task numbers, and saved-task loading.

Integrate the first OOP refactoring iteration, extracting task parsing
and task-number validation into Parser. All five UI regression cases
pass on Java 25. Ui and TaskList extraction remain for later iterations.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add keyword search for task descriptions
commitResults.messageBody:
Users currently need to scan the entire list to locate related tasks.
Add find with case-insensitive substring matching on descriptions only.
Preserve task order and status, number the results independently, and
report missing keywords and empty results without modifying tasks.

Extend the UI plan to cover all task types, phrases, mixed case,
nonmatching dates, invalid input, and unchanged list state.
All six UI regression cases pass on Java 25.

Deliver keyword search with description-only matching and validated
UI behavior for the Level-9 increment.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document Java APIs and refresh Dog responses
commitResults.messageBody:
Add Javadoc for public APIs and private helpers so their purpose,
parameters, return values, and failure conditions are easier to follow.

Include the user's response wording and formatting edits. Update the UI
plan to reflect the intentional wording changes rather than reverting
those customizations. All six UI regression cases pass on Java 25.

Replace the starter documentation with setup instructions, command
syntax and examples, task-status explanations, and troubleshooting.

Explain description-only search, result numbering, free-form dates,
and automatic persistence so users can operate Dog confidently.
Set the guide permalink to the Pages root for publication from docs.

Replace the starter guide with setup steps, command examples, search
numbering guidance, persistence details, and troubleshooting advice.
Include the user's closing message and prepare the guide for publication
at the GitHub Pages root.

Reconcile the earlier published guide with the revised local commit.
Resolve the closing-line conflict by preserving the user's message.

Dog still owned console output, input, and the mutable task collection.
Extract Ui and TaskList so each concern has a dedicated class, and move
command argument parsing into Parser. Keep existing command responses.

Handle end of input as a clean exit, document all public APIs, wrap long
message declarations, and correct storage indentation. Report mutation
success only after saving succeeds. All six UI cases and Javadoc checks
pass on Java 25.

Complete the Ui and TaskList extraction through pull request #1.
Keep the feature branch and a distinct merge commit for the increment.
